questions.stem: Which of HBr (hydrobromic acid), HCl (hydrochloric acid), HCN (hydrocyanic acid), or NH4+ (ammonium) is the strongest acid?

options.misconception: HCl: chloride is stabilized by chlorine's high electronegativity, so HCl is stronger than weak acids
HCN: cyanide is only weakly stabilized and carbon is not very electronegative
ammonium: nitrogen holds its proton fairly tightly, so it is a weak acid

questions.explanation: Among HBr (hydrobromic acid),HCl (hydrochloric acid),HCN (hydrocyanic acid),NH4+ (ammonium), HBr (hydrobromic acid) is the strongest acid because its conjugate base is the most stabilized, which lowers its pKa and favors proton loss.
questions.hint: The strongest acid has the lowest pKa and the most stabilized conjugate base.
